title: AWS Cloud Foundations
tagline: Move a real website to AWS safely, cheaply and without the jargon fog.
description: Most AWS courses start with a list of two hundred services. This one starts with a website. Lantern is a small events site running on one rented server, and over fourteen lessons you move it to AWS: a locked-down account with a budget alarm, people and code with exactly the permissions they need, and the right compute, storage, database and network pieces for each job.

Every lesson treats cost and security as part of the design, not an afterthought. You learn to read IAM policies line by line, drive AWS from the AWS CLI v2, host a static site on Amazon S3 behind Amazon CloudFront, build a serverless API with AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway and Amazon DynamoDB, and watch it all with Amazon CloudWatch.
audience: Developers and career switchers who can use a terminal and want to run real workloads on AWS with confidence.
prerequisites: Comfort with a command line and a basic idea of how a website talks to a server; no AWS experience needed.
learnItems: Lock down a new AWS account with MFA, an admin user and a budget
Explain Regions, Availability Zones and the shared responsibility model
Read and write least-privilege IAM policies with conditions
Choose between EC2 and Lambda, S3, EBS and EFS, RDS and DynamoDB
Design a VPC with public and private subnets and tight security groups
Ship a static site and serverless API, then monitor and cost-review them
